note: A fresh 'phase_measure_theory' restart of the whole KnowledgeOS investigation from Question 1: formally defines Observation as a tuple of target/reality, purpose, observer, access, context, time, and selection, with Observation != Reality and Observation != Knowledge; revised into ObsAct=(T,P,Ao,Ac,C,tau,S,M) after separating observer from access and reality from target.

This batch's working formalization of Dimension as a semantic axis distinct from Statement and Value, developed via the Bhishma-relationship test case; argues dimensions need not be primitive, proposes an eight-field Relationship structure as a first-class construct, and finds the bare (Entity,Dimension,Value) triple insufficient (needs epistemic status/evidence/temporal validity).

Principle that investigation depth is not fixed by the initial question but emerges dynamically from dimensions/relationships discovered during observation; proposes six investigation levels (initial observation through decision investigation) and an architectural investigation loop (Question->Observation->Dimension Discovery->Zero/Lord Lens->more investigation?->Guidance).

Epistemic capability complementary to Zero Lens: while Zero detects known boundaries/gaps in the current knowledge state, Lord suggests candidate dimensions/horizons that could exist beyond current knowledge, expanding rather than merely auditing the investigation space.

The proposed KnowledgeOS role that determines what the Knower should investigate or do next, given the current epistemic state, Zero's detected gaps, and Lord's candidate dimensions; distinct from Zero (detection) and Lord (expansion), and from the human Knower who retains understanding/decision/action.

This batch's operational, mathematically-signed formalization of Zero Lens as a function from knowledge states to a set of epistemic boundary findings (unknown values, conflicts, unvalidated assumptions, unresolved findings), with explicit constraints that it neither prioritizes gaps nor determines truth, and does not itself claim to enumerate unknown-unknowns (that is Lord's job). Registered as a new OBJECT-level entry distinct from the THEORY-LEVEL z-kos-001-zero-principle meta-principle (B0007), though relation is possibly the same underlying Zero concept made operational; flagged POSSIBLY rather than merged because this batch's exchange treats Zero as freshly (re)defined from scratch without citing the earlier registrations.

KnowledgeOS capability that derives candidate semantic dimensions from a Knower's natural-language intent, context, domain ontology, observation, Zero gaps, Lord horizons and learned patterns, without requiring the Knower to name dimensions explicitly; includes the Semantic Reconstruction sub-capability (structural + semantic-role parsing) and an explicit DimensionAssessment step separating candidate from adopted dimensions. Distinct from the pre-existing dimension-discovery-uncertainty object (B0017), which is about known-vs-unknown-dimension uncertainty rather than this batch's parsing/discovery pipeline.

The decision to recommend Rust (optionally with Tree-sitter for structural parsing) as the implementation technology for the Semantic Reconstruction/parsing engine, chosen for memory safety, determinism, and the ability to represent a typed semantic structure that preserves unresolved/ambiguous elements explicitly rather than silently guessing; paired with the constraint that an LLM used within this pipeline is an optional analytical provider, never itself a source of truth (LLM != Knowledge).

aliases: Mathematical Review of the KnowledgeOS Model
note: A full audit of the phase_measure_theory KnowledgeOS model-so-far (Observation, Dimension, Statement, Value, Relationship, Evidence, Epistemic Status, Temporal Validity, and the Semantic Reconstruction/Dimension Discovery/Zero/Lord/Sarathi capabilities), producing an itemized list of unformalized gaps (no evidence model, no epistemic-status transition algebra, no value-space formalization, no temporal logic, incomplete Statement structure) and a methodological correction against declaring the model complete.

The proposed smallest meaningful unit of KnowledgeOS knowledge (Entity,Dimension,Value,TemporalValidity,EpistemicStatus,Evidence,Provenance) with Compare/Challenge/Update/Preserve operations; superseded within the same file by the proposition-assertion-knowledge-hierarchy, which reclassifies it as an Assertion rather than raw Knowledge.

Three(later four)-level epistemic hierarchy: Proposition (semantic content) subset-of Assertion (proposition + epistemic commitment/evidence/provenance) subset-of Knowledge (justified assertion), with a correction that KnowledgeOS can only ever reach a Truth Assessment, never absolute Truth/Reality itself.

Formal model of Evidence as input to an epistemic-state transition function, including a numeric support/strength calculus later flagged as an unvalidated experimental candidate (no evidence-independence/correlation model).

The Compare and Challenge operations over Assertions (and, after correction, separately over Propositions vs Assertions), used by Zero (gap detection), Lord (alternative generation) and Sarathi (investigation guidance).

notations: Logical Contradiction != Semantic Incompatibility != Temporal Difference != Contextual Difference != Normative Conflict != Decision Conflict
note: A six-member taxonomy distinguishing kinds of apparent conflict between assertions, motivated by the Bhishma grandfather/teacher/opponent case: only true logical contradiction (P and not-P) is a falsification-relevant conflict; the rest (semantic incompatibility, temporal/contextual difference, normative conflict, decision conflict) can coexist as simultaneously true/valid without either assertion being false.

The Update and Preserve operations on Assertions: versioning, provenance chains, and a corrected (non-linear, world-state-vs-epistemic-history-separated) lifecycle model, including the Retired-vs-Rejected and Proposition-Identity-vs-Assertion-Version distinctions.

The complete Knowledge State schema (Assertions, Relationships, Evidence, History, Zero findings, Lord candidates) as a knowledge graph, later corrected to require Observer/Purpose/Context parameterization and to resolve a circularity from embedding Zero(K_t) and History inside K_t itself; paired with a System State that also includes the Ideal State and current inquiry.

The batch's full-model synthesis document (Lord/Krishna/KnowledgeOS/Knower architecture plus every prior definition and invariant), immediately followed by a review refusing to accept it as complete and setting a six-question research agenda (Coherence/Conflict/Resolution/Gap/Ideal-State/Distance) plus a prioritized 'what is Knowledge itself' question.

notations: K_P subset K_A subset K_J subset K_t subset Omega (rejected)
note: Attempt to define Knowledge itself as a layered concept across five levels (Knowledge Space, Propositional, Assertional, Epistemically-Accepted, Knowledge State), immediately corrected for a subset-hierarchy category error and for using 'justified true belief' despite KnowledgeOS having no access to Truth; replaced by a typed composition hierarchy and a purpose/context-relative Accepted(K,P,C) predicate.

Full ten-type formal type system for the KnowledgeOS epistemic model, resolving the containment-vs-set-inclusion category error from Question 7 by giving every prior object (Observation, Dimension, Proposition, Assertion, Evidence, EpistemicState, Relationship, KnowledgeState, KnowledgeSpace) an explicit type and typed operation signatures for Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Compare/Challenge/Update/Preserve.

notations: Coherent(K_t)=Logical(K_t) and Epistemic(K_t) and Temporal(K_t) and Contextual(K_t) and Structural(K_t)
note: Defines Coherence of a Knowledge State as a conjunction of five well-formedness predicates, explicitly distinct from conflict-freedom, completeness, adequacy, and truth; made relational to purpose/context/time/ruleset.

Defines Conflict with five initial types later corrected to a content-conflict-plus-applicable-frame model, splits assertion-level from implication-level conflict, and introduces Reframe as a third mode (beside evidence acquisition and dimension discovery) by which KnowledgeOS resolves epistemic tension without picking a winning assertion.

Defines Gap as distinct from Conflict, corrected from 'absence' to 'insufficiency relative to a purpose/context/time-generated knowledge requirement R(P,C,t)'; shows gaps and conflicts can transform into each other as new dimensions/context are discovered, and extends Zero's output to a Gap/Conflict/epistemic-Boundary triple.

This batch's own re-derivation of the Ideal State as the Knower's target model against which Knowledge/Understanding/Domain-reality are each compared, split into I^K/I^U/I^D forms; flagged as possibly related to the pre-existing ideal-state-comparison-model (B0017) but developed independently within this phase_measure_theory thread without citing it.

The model of epistemic/understanding/domain distance between a current state and its Ideal, corrected from a naive scalar/norm framing to a Difference(Compare)/Deficit(Severity)/Distance(Measure) three-level hierarchy, with the safety invariant that current knowledge must never be allowed to silently redefine its own target.

KnowledgeOS's event-sourcing state-transition model: an eight-theorem (T1-T8) architecture separating Operation/Command from Event from state Transition, requiring only committed events to change the Knowledge State, with append-only History and state reconstruction via Replay.

The transition rules governing how an Assertion's epistemic state changes under Observe/AddEvidence/Infer/AssessUncertainty, converged (after removing Conflict and Resolution as external relational/process objects) to a four-dimensional Sigma_A vector, explicitly non-monotonic and not forming a lattice.

The layered architecture connecting the three epistemic lenses to the Question-15 event-sourcing transition system: Zero/Lord/Sarathi form an analytical guidance cycle producing recommendations only, strictly separated from a subsequent Authorization boundary (Knower/policy decides), Execution boundary (command attempted, may fail), and Transition boundary (validated event mutates Knowledge State); guidance is explicitly optional, not a prerequisite for every transition.

The batch's final synthesized KnowledgeOS system-state model: an eight-component persistent state (Knowledge/Understanding/Domain/Ideal/Inquiry/Context/Knower/Policy) with all analysis (Zero/discrepancy), guidance (Lord/Sarathi), and governance (Decision/Authorization) layers modelled as pure functional projections over that state rather than stored fields, closing with a five-bounded-context DDD partition and an explicit retraction of any claim to a complete mathematical specification.

The closing question of the phase_measure_theory investigation: how KnowledgeOS orders candidate resolution opportunities (not raw deficiencies) for action, corrected from a compensable weighted-sum scalar to a policy-governed, dependency-graph-constrained ordering over Resolution Opportunity objects, with Finding != Action as the key structural distinction.
